rationale:
Evidence: iteration 0 (kp 2.5, kd 0.3, ki 0.1, base 1.8, 10 mm sensor pitch) went off track in all 60 trials. Progress was 0.13 to 0.20, rms_error 0.02 to 0.03, max_error 0.06 at the off-track limit, and steering_oscillation 0.11 to 0.16. Oscillation is the clearest symptom, and the robot leaves the line before it reaches the finish. No run has completed, so completion (500 points) is still unproven.

The round-2 critique is right on the main point. My previous revision claimed the geometry was unchanged, but it moved sensor pitch from the tested 10 mm to 12 mm. I reject that change and return to the tested 10 mm layout. That way this race is a clean test of the controller changes, and any gain in progress can be attributed to them.

Changed: (1) kp 2.5 to 2.0. Oscillation is the dominant failure, and at signal 2 the turn term is 5 x 350 = 1750 PWM at kp 2.5, which overshoots the line. A 20% cut is a modest step that keeps some correction on bends. (2) kd 0.3 to 0.5. This adds damping against the overshoot that produced the oscillation. The derivative noise gain rises, but 0.5 was the original value and is within the range I can justify without a noise test. (3) base_speed 1.8 to 1.5. Lower speed gives the controller more time per bend and reduces the chance of leaving the line on the sharpest slalom bends. Completion inside 3 s is less likely, so this is a trade-off. I accept it because a finish requires staying on the line first, and the time term is worth at most 60 points. (4) ki 0.1 to 0.05, to reduce integral windup on bends, which the critique flagged as a risk. The integral is clamped at +/-2 and the motor mismatch is about 2%, so ki 0.05 still gives a small correction.

Kept: five 12 mm sensors, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction line loss, wheel_track 0.12, body_width 0.12, body_length 0.18, mass 0.8, wheel_radius 0.03. These are neutral choices or were not varied.

Rejected: raising kp above 2.0 without evidence. The critique's stability estimate is unverified, and oscillation is already too high.

I am changing four controller values at once, so the next telemetry cannot isolate each effect. I accept that and prioritise a first finish over clean attribution. Expected result (unverified): fewer line_loss_events, lower steering_oscillation (below 0.1), progress above 0.3, and possibly an oval finish. Next-step rule: if oscillation is still above 0.1 with max_error at 0.06, lower kp by 0.5. If the oval finishes slowly (completion_time above 2.5 s), raise base_speed by 0.2. If progress stalls below 0.5 with low oscillation, raise kp by 0.5.
